root_cause: After round 1, CBMC still reports 'arithmetic overflow on signed division in num / den' (safe_ratio.overflow.1, src/safe_ratio.c line 8) with num = INT_MIN (-2147483648) and den = -1: the mathematical quotient 2147483648 is not representable as an int, which is undefined behaviour in C. UBSan confirms it in the int_min_by_minus_one test ('division of -2147483648 by -1 cannot be represented in type int').
rationale: INT_MIN / -1 is the only int division that overflows, so check exactly that pair before dividing and return SAFE_RATIO_ERR_OVERFLOW without writing *out (POST3). The checks are written out in the order the contract specifies: out == NULL, then den == 0, then INT_MIN / -1; every remaining pair has a representable quotient.
